status: BLOCKED on a reproducibility guard — diagnosis narrowed 2026-09-15
what_happened: T6 refused to write a result. Its guard requires the UNCAPPED rung of the span ladder to reproduce the published eval.json EER to within TOL=1e-6, because a capped EER is only interpretable against an uncapped one from the same code path.
diagnosis: The difference is 0.010082 pp, and one trial out of 19,838 is 0.005041 pp -- so EXACTLY 2 TRIALS flipped. That is floating-point nondeterminism across GPU architectures, not a rebuild error: 231 tensors loaded in both runs from the same checkpoint. MFAConformer_full_si_s42 was originally scored on compute-node-4's A40 (dispatch_state.json records slot compute-node-4:gpu0); the probe ran on compute-node-1's T4. Different card, different cuDNN kernel selection and reduction order, two borderline trials cross the threshold.
the_guard_is_correct: It should NOT be disabled. It exists so a capped number is never compared against an uncapped one from a different code path -- exactly the defect class the evaluation-integrity rebuild of 22 August closed. What it did not anticipate is the probe running on different silicon from the scorer.

resolutions.action: Run the probe on an A40 (the card that produced the published number)
Re-score T1 on the T4 first (evaluate_transformer --redo), so the baseline and the probe come from the same card, THEN probe
resolutions.caution: must not overwrite the published eval.json -- T1's 4.950 is quoted in the annual report

resolutions.action: Widen TOL to a documented cross-hardware value (>= 2 trials = 0.0101 pp)
resolutions.caution: weakens a guard that is otherwise doing real work; only with the hardware reason written into the code

incidental_finding: Cross-GPU reproducibility of this benchmark is +/-0.01 pp (2 trials in 19,838) between an A40 and a T4 on an identical checkpoint. Worth recording: the programme's power analysis says differences below ~2 pp are not resolvable anyway, so this is far inside the noise floor -- but any future claim of EXACT reproduction must name the GPU.
prediction_P22_status: STILL NOT SCORED — the probe has produced no capped numbers

round2.what_was_tried: A3 was patched to re-score T1 on the SAME card before probing, on the hypothesis that the 2-trial gap was A40-vs-T4 floating point. It ran three more times and failed identically.
round2.decisive_observation: The delta is EXACTLY 0.010082 pp every time — attempt 1 on an A40-scored baseline, and attempts 2-3 against a freshly T4-scored baseline. A hardware FP difference would vary run to run. A bit-reproducible delta is a SYSTEMATIC path difference, so the cross-hardware explanation is WRONG and is withdrawn.

hypotheses_ruled_out.ruled_out_by: delta identical after re-scoring on the same card

hypotheses_ruled_out.h: the scorer passes cohort=, the probe does not
hypotheses_ruled_out.ruled_out_by: evaluate.py:367-368 computes the cosine metric BEFORE any cohort work; cohort cannot reach the cosine EER

hypotheses_ruled_out.h: set_attention(model,'full') differs from the as-constructed path
hypotheses_ruled_out.ruled_out_by: attn.py set_mode() assigns only self.mode/window/kv_stride and touches no parameter; for a model trained with --arm full it is a no-op

round2.remaining_hypothesis: 0.010082 pp is exactly 2 trials of 19,838 (100/19838 = 0.0050408). The most likely remaining cause is TIE-BREAKING in the EER threshold search: if trials share a score, a different embedding-extraction order changes which side of the threshold they land on. The probe calls span_profile(model, x) — a forward pass over its own sampled batch — before the ladder, which is the one ordering difference left between the two paths.
round2.next_step: Test it directly and cheaply: run ev.evaluate_set twice on the same loaded model, once with and once without a preceding span_profile() call, and compare the cosine EER. If they differ by the same 2 trials, the cause is confirmed and the guard's TOL=1e-6 is stricter than the EER statistic's own reproducibility under reordering.
round2.decision_required: If confirmed: widen TOL to a documented value (>= 3 trials, 0.0151 pp) WITH the reason written into the code. Do NOT loosen it silently — the guard exists so a capped EER is never compared against an uncapped one from a different code path, which is the defect class the 22 August evaluation-integrity rebuild closed.
